articles.title: Hero Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition Launched at Rs 1.16 Lakh
articles.categoryDescription: Recent news and new launches: vehicles, gadgets, AI and aviation, explained from official sources.
articles.excerpt: Hero MotoCorp launched the Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition on 6 November 2026 at Rs 1,16,250 ex-showroom, with a colour TFT display and a tyre pressure monitoring system.
blocks: Hero MotoCorp launched the Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition on 6 November 2026 at Rs 1,16,250 (ex-showroom, pan-India). It is the new top variant of the Xtreme 125R and the only one with a 4.2-inch colour TFT instrument display and a tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS). This article is based on reports dated 6 November 2026 and is correct as of 10 November 2026.

According to Autocar Professional, which reported Hero's announcement, the TFT cluster has Bluetooth connectivity. Once a phone is paired, it can show turn-by-turn navigation prompts, call and SMS alerts and control music playback. Autocar India adds that the same 4.2-inch unit is used on other Hero models such as the Xtreme 160R, Xtreme 250R Carbon and Xpulse 210.

The tyre pressure monitoring system gives real-time pressure information and alerts. Hero describes it as a segment-first feature, meaning the first in the 125cc class. Both outlets say no other Xtreme 125R variant has the TFT or the TPMS.

Display: 4.2-inch colour TFT with Bluetooth
Safety: tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS)
Look: Midnight Black with Pearl Red accents and coloured alloy wheels (Autocar India describes a bronze-and-black scheme with red wheels)
Carried over: dual-channel ABS, three ride modes (Rain, Road, Sport) and cruise control, per Autocar Professional

Autocar India says Hero did not mention cruise control in its press release, but notes that the dual-channel ABS variant below already has it. Autocar Professional lists it among the carried-over features. Readers should check the feature list with a dealer.

Autocar India reports that the Stealth Edition is mechanically the same as the other Xtreme 125R variants. The engine is a 124.7cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled unit that makes 11.4 hp and 10.5 Nm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox. Hero has not announced any change to these figures.
Price and the rest of the range
Autocar India says the Xtreme 125R now comes in five variants. It lists these ex-showroom prices, rounded as the outlet printed them:

CBS: Rs 91,500
ABS: Rs 96,700
ABS single-seat: Rs 96,700
Dual-channel ABS: Rs 1.10 lakh
Stealth Edition: Rs 1.16 lakh (Rs 1,16,250 exact, per Autocar Professional)

Autocar India puts the gap to the dual-channel ABS variant at about Rs 6,000. That figure uses the rounded Rs 1.10 lakh, so the exact difference may be slightly larger. Prices are ex-showroom; on-road prices add insurance, registration and other charges and differ by city.
How it compares by published prices

Autocar India names two rivals in the 125cc sport class: the TVS Raider, priced from Rs 84,460 to Rs 1.03 lakh, and the Honda CB125 Hornet at Rs 1.15 lakh. By those published numbers, the Stealth Edition is priced about Rs 1,250 above the Hornet figure quoted, though the two bikes differ in equipment and the outlet's figures may not be from the same date.

Autocar Professional quotes Ashutosh Varma, Chief Business Officer for Hero MotoCorp's India Business Unit: the new edition 'further raises the bar by making connected technology and intelligent safety features even more accessible'. The company has not published delivery timelines in the reports reviewed, and the bike is available at dealerships nationwide according to Autocar Professional.

The reports describe features and prices, not ownership experience, so several points are left to a dealer or Hero's website: the warranty terms for the TFT and the TPMS sensors, whether the Stealth Edition is sold in colours other than the single Midnight Black scheme, and booking and delivery timelines. Hero has also not said whether it will add the TFT or TPMS to the lower variants later.

One more detail is worth noting: Autocar India describes the colour scheme as bronze and black with red wheels, while Autocar Professional says Midnight Black with Pearl Red accents. The outlets describe the same single finish in different words, so the safest reading is a dark bike with red highlights on the wheels, grab rails and the X in the badge.

Hero's own press release could not be opened for this article. The facts above come from two trade outlets, Autocar India and Autocar Professional, that agree on the price, display, TPMS and variant count. Check hero motocorp's website or a dealer before buying.

sources.title: Hero MotoCorp Launches Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition with TFT at Rs 1.16 Lakh, Autocar Professional
Hero Xtreme 125R Stealth Edition launched at Rs 1.16 lakh, Autocar India

articles.title: TVS Leads India Electric Two-Wheeler Sales in Oct 2026
articles.excerpt: FADA data shows 2,24,064 electric two-wheelers were retailed in India in October 2026, up 48.5% on a year earlier, with TVS first at 60,490 units.
blocks: India retailed 2,24,064 electric two-wheelers in October 2026, which is 48.5% more than in October 2025, according to data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). TVS Motor was the top brand with 60,490 units, up 94.7% year on year. This article reports figures published on 6 and 9 November 2026 and is correct as of 10 November 2026.
Autocar Professional and Business Today both report the FADA ranking. Retail sales are registrations, meaning vehicles handed over to customers, not dispatches from factories.

TVS Motor: 60,490 units, up 94.7% (31,075 units in October 2025)
Bajaj Auto: 49,126 units, up 51.3%
Ather Energy: 31,833 units, up 5.3%
Hero MotoCorp: 29,923 units, up 81.4%
Ola Electric: 12,098 units, down 26.4%
Greaves Electric Mobility: 10,839 units
River Mobility: 6,817 units, up 273.9%

Business Today notes that Ola Electric was the only one of the top five brands to record a fall on the year. Autocar India adds that Ola's October figure was also 10.1% lower than its September 2026 number.

Electric models made up 9.7% of all two-wheeler retail sales in October 2026. In September 2026 the share was 11.6%, and in October 2025 it was 4.7% according to Business Today. The share fell from September even though the number of electric units rose about 8% month on month, from 2,07,314 to 2,24,064.

Autocar Professional and Autocar India both link the lower share to the timing of Diwali. The festival fell in October in 2025 but falls in November in 2026, so a large part of festive buying has moved out of the month. Overall two-wheeler retail sales fell about 28% on the year to roughly 23.21 lakh units in October, according to Autocar Professional's report on the same FADA release. A smaller total with a similar electric volume produces a smaller electric share, not necessarily weaker electric demand.

For context, trade coverage of the same FADA release reports 88,570 electric three-wheelers retailed in October 2026, up 24.76% from 70,995 a year earlier. That figure was not checked against FADA's own tables for this article.

Retail means registered with transport offices (Vahan records), so it lags factory dispatches
Year-on-year gains compare against October 2025, when Diwali buying fell inside the month
Percentages are the outlets' rounding of FADA data
Brand lists cover the largest sellers, not every maker

Business Today says the data was collated on 4 November 2026 from 1,468 of the country's 1,469 regional transport offices, according to FADA Research. Later corrections to registrations could change the final numbers slightly.
What changed compared with a year ago

Four of the top five brands grew on the year, according to Autocar India. TVS almost doubled, Hero grew by more than four-fifths, Bajaj by about half, and Ather by a modest five per cent. Ather's own cumulative total for 2026 is covered by Autocar India in a separate report, which says it passed 3.01 lakh units between 1 January and 6 November 2026 on Vahan data.
The share of electric models in total two-wheeler sales was 4.7% in October 2025 and 9.7% in October 2026, so the share roughly doubled across the year even after the dip from September.

Retail data counts customer deliveries, and two-wheeler purchases cluster around festivals. When Diwali moves from October to November, deliveries move with it. Comparing one October with another October that held Diwali therefore understates the underlying change. The sources do not say what November will show, and nothing here is a forecast.

FADA's own press release could not be opened for this article. The figures come from Autocar Professional and Business Today, which agree with each other, and Autocar India for the month-on-month comparison for Ola. This is general information about sales data, not advice on any purchase.

sources.title: TVS Doubles Sales to Lead Electric Two-Wheeler Market as Diwali Calendar Shift Dips Penetration, Autocar Professional
EV two-wheeler sales jump 48% in October, electric car registrations surge 76%, Business Today
TVS leads electric two-wheeler sales in October 2026 as sales nearly double, Autocar India

articles.title: Electric Car Sales Reach 37,049 in India in Oct 2026
articles.excerpt: FADA data shows 37,049 electric cars were retailed in India in October 2026, up 76.5% on a year earlier. Tata led with 14,669 units, followed by Mahindra and MG.
blocks: Electric passenger vehicle retail sales in India reached 37,049 units in October 2026, up 76.47% from 20,995 in October 2025, according to data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA). Tata Motors led with 14,669 units. This article reports figures published on 6 and 9 November 2026 and is correct as of 10 November 2026.
Autocar India published the brand table from FADA's data, and Business Today reported the leading names. They agree on the top of the list.

Tata: 14,669 units, up 77.6% on a year earlier
Mahindra: 8,538 units, up 85.7%
MG: 5,939 units, up 10.8%
VinFast: 2,571 units (142 in October 2025, per Business Today)
Kia: 1,395 units, up 85.3%
Maruti Suzuki: 1,200 units
Hyundai: 760 units, up 42.3%
BYD: 737 units, up 4.1%
BMW: 462 units, up 26.6%
Tesla: 291 units (40 in October 2025)
Toyota: 190 units
Mercedes: 62 units, down 48.8%
Citroen: 60 units
Volvo: 37 units
Autocar India says domestic rivals are narrowing the gap to Tata. Mahindra's 8,538 units compare with 4,599 in October 2025, per the same outlet.

Electric cars made up 7.3% of passenger vehicle retail sales in October 2026. That is more than double the 3.5% of October 2025, but lower than the 8.5% of September 2026. Autocar India reports that overall car sales fell 14% on the year in October, which lowers the denominator and also interacts with timing: Diwali fell in November this year, not October.

Business Today reports that electric passenger vehicle sales rose 2.61% from September to October. The share therefore dipped because total car registrations rose faster than electric ones in the month, not because electric registrations fell.
What the figures do not show

They are retail registrations, not factory dispatches or orders
They count passenger vehicles in FADA's data only, not electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers or commercial vehicles
Prices, range and model mix per brand are not part of the release
Figures may be revised as late registrations come in
Business Today says the data was collated on 4 November 2026 from 1,468 of the country's 1,469 regional transport offices, according to FADA Research.
Electric two-wheeler figures from the same release are covered in a separate news article, and a guide to how a battery electric car works is in the Cars and Bikes category.

Several brands in the table grew from very small bases, so large percentages need care. VinFast's 2,571 units compare with 142 a year earlier, which is an increase of about eighteen times, and Tesla's 291 compare with 40. By contrast, Tata's growth of 77.6% came on a base of thousands of cars. Autocar India notes that Maruti Suzuki, with 1,200 units, has no year-earlier figure in the table, because it had no comparable electric model on sale in October 2025.

Business Today puts Tata Passenger Electric Mobility, Mahindra and JSW MG Motor India at the top in that order. Together the three brands account for 29,146 of the 37,049 units, a little under four-fifths. That sum is calculated here from the published figures.

Autocar India's table shows how brands moved from September to October 2026. Mahindra rose 9.74%, MG 13.30% and Kia 10.54%, while Tata slipped 0.82%, VinFast fell 13.26%, BYD fell 11.84% and Mercedes fell 50.40%. Month-on-month changes can reflect supply, launches and promotions as well as demand, and the sources do not give reasons for individual brands.

FADA publishes monthly retail reports covering passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, three-wheelers, commercial vehicles, tractors and construction equipment. Readers who need exact figures for research should use the federation's release, since press coverage rounds some numbers.
FADA's own release could not be opened for this article. Numbers come from Autocar India and Business Today, which agree on every brand figure compared. Percentages are the outlets' rounding.

sources.title: Electric car retail sales surge 76 percent in October 2026, Autocar India
EV two-wheeler sales jump 48% in October, electric car registrations surge 76%, Business Today

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 2,814 Crore Critical Minerals Scheme
articles.excerpt: On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet approved a Rs 2,814 crore scheme giving 30% capital support for four lithium and nickel processing plants from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
blocks: On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing, with a financial outlay of Rs 2,814 crore over five years. According to the official release published on the Prime Minister's website, it targets the processing of lithium and nickel. This article is correct as of 10 November 2026.
The scheme runs from the financial year 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under it, the government will provide a capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment for four critical mineral processing plants.

Two lithium processing plants, each with a minimum capacity of 30 kt
Two nickel processing plants, each with a minimum capacity of 50 kt
Maximum support: Rs 500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs 900 crore per nickel beneficiary
Total outlay: Rs 2,814 crore
The release says the scheme targets turning lithium and nickel ores and intermediate products into high-purity compounds. Cobalt is expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production.

The release describes a two-stage process. In the first stage, applications are assessed for technical qualification. Only technically qualified applicants take part in the second stage, a financial bid. For each mineral, two beneficiaries are selected on a least-cost basis, which means the bidders asking for the lowest capital support. The incentive is paid in three tranches linked to milestones.
Why the government gave for the scheme

The release states that processing of critical minerals is concentrated in a few places worldwide, which exposes supply chains to disruption, price swings and possible restrictions. It says India depends substantially on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials because domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure is at an early stage. It adds that commercial-scale projects face high capital needs, limited access to suitable technology and constrained raw materials.

The release names electric mobility, battery energy storage systems, electronics, defence and speciality steel as sectors that would be supported. It links the scheme to the Atmanirbhar Bharat objective.

Business Today reported that the same Cabinet meeting also approved a Rs 14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage and the Rs 4,371.10 crore VISTAR statistics scheme. Those are covered in separate articles on this site.

When applications will open and the dates of the bidding stages
Which companies or locations will take part
The quantity of lithium and nickel compounds the four plants must produce, beyond the minimum capacities
Any response from opposition parties or industry bodies; none was found in the sources reviewed, and none is included

A critical mineral is one the government considers important to the economy or security and exposed to supply risk. Processing means turning mined ore into the high-purity chemicals that battery and electronics makers can use; it is a separate step from mining. Capital expenditure (capex) support means the government pays part of the cost of building a plant, here 30% of eligible investment, instead of subsidising the products it makes.

Least-cost bidding means companies compete on how little support they ask for. If one lithium bidder asks for 25% and another asks for 30%, the lower request wins, within the cap of Rs 500 crore per lithium beneficiary. The release does not give examples, so the percentages here are an illustration of the method and not a forecast of any bid.

The release says the support is meant for companies that build processing plants and, through them, the sectors that use the compounds. Ordinary consumers are not given any payment or price change by this decision. Any effect on the cost of batteries or electric vehicles would depend on what the plants produce and when, and the release makes no such claim.

The Press Information Bureau page could not be opened. The details above come from the release as published on the Prime Minister's website, and the headline figures were matched with Business Today's report of the Cabinet briefing. This article reports the decision as announced and is not updated after publication.

sources.title: Cabinet Approves Capex Support Scheme for Critical Mineral Processing, Prime Minister of India
Cabinet approves Rs 14,500 cr energy storage scheme and VISTAR plan, Business Today

articles.title: Yangwang Altior Luxury Sedan Unveiled in Abu Dhabi
articles.excerpt: BYD's Yangwang brand unveiled the 5.6-metre Altior sedan in Abu Dhabi on 7 November 2026 and opened pre-orders for a 399-unit limited edition.
blocks: Yangwang, the ultra-luxury brand of BYD, unveiled its Altior executive flagship sedan in Abu Dhabi on Saturday, 7 November 2026, according to CnEVPost. Pre-orders opened for a limited edition capped at 399 units worldwide, with an expected price of 2,080,000 yuan that is not yet final. No India launch has been announced. This article is correct as of 10 November 2026.

CnEVPost reports the Altior is 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide and 1,590 mm tall, with a 3,500 mm wheelbase. Autocar India, which describes the same car, says the design is inspired by the 'ding', an ancient Chinese ceremonial bronze vessel, according to BYD, and that Altior comes from the Latin word for higher.

Doors: rear coach doors hinged at the back; both outlets say they open close to 90 degrees and hold umbrellas
Wheels: 21-inch, on 275/45 tyres (Autocar India)
Paint: two-tone finish with a darker bonnet and roof (Autocar India)
Seating: four seats in the launch layout; a five-seat version will follow (CnEVPost)

Autocar India reports yellow Hetian jade detailing on the air vents, Suzhou silk embroidery, a 39-speaker Dynaudio sound system and rear 'zero-gravity' seats with a massage function. It also lists a 21.4-inch overhead screen and two fridges. CnEVPost lists wood trim, metal accents, electric privacy sunshades and champagne glass holders in the official images. These are manufacturer claims, relayed by the outlets.

CnEVPost says the car uses BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and flash charging, with a CLTC-rated range above 1,000 km. CLTC is China's test cycle, and its figures are usually higher than those from other test cycles such as WLTP. The outlets differ on one point: Autocar India calls the Altior all-electric, while CnEVPost notes that Yangwang has not explicitly said whether it is a hybrid or pure-electric vehicle. Treat the powertrain type as unconfirmed.

CnEVPost says the first version open for pre-order is the four-seat Shanhe Dingyun limited edition. It needs a deposit of 300,000 yuan in China (about 44,660 US dollars, per CnEVPost) and carries an expected price of 2,080,000 yuan. Autocar India refers to Executive and Bespoke editions. The two outlets use different edition names, and BYD's own edition list was not opened.

Autocar India describes the car as a Rolls-Royce Phantom rival. CnEVPost names the Maybach S-Class and Bentley Flying Spur as the models it competes with. Both comparisons are the outlets' framing, not figures from a test.

Delivery dates and final price
Whether the car will be sold in India or in the UAE, where it was unveiled
Powertrain type and battery size
Five-seat version pricing
CnEVPost adds that Yangwang's cumulative sales were 3,546 units in the first ten months of 2026, based on its own data compilation.

Yangwang is the ultra-luxury brand of BYD, which is listed in Hong Kong. According to CnEVPost, its existing sedan, the U7, comes in plug-in hybrid and battery-electric versions, and the brand launched the four-seat flagship SUV U8L Dingcang Edition in August 2026. Autocar India says the Altior gets a fully active body control system and the God's Eye A driver assistance features, which it describes as BYD's claims.

A note on units: the 300,000 yuan deposit and the 2,080,000 yuan expected price are Chinese-market figures. CnEVPost converts the deposit to about 44,660 US dollars. No Indian rupee price exists, because no India launch has been announced.

Because the outlets disagree on edition names and the powertrain, and because no price in any market other than the expected Chinese figure has been published, readers should treat this as an early unveiling report. Specifications, trims and prices can change before deliveries start, and the sources reviewed here do not say when that will be.
BYD's press release could not be opened. Details come from CnEVPost and Autocar India, which agree on the unveiling, dimensions and coach doors but differ on edition names and powertrain wording.

articles.title: How a Car Alternator Charges the Battery While Driving
articles.excerpt: An alternator is a belt-driven generator that keeps a car's battery charged and runs its electrics. See how its rotor, stator, rectifier and regulator work together.
blocks: A car's alternator is a small generator turned by the engine through a belt. It charges the battery and powers the lights, wipers, screens and other electrics while the engine runs. Inside, a spinning electromagnet makes alternating current in fixed coils, a set of diodes turns that into direct current, and a regulator keeps the voltage steady. This article follows The Engineering Mindset's guide and Wikipedia's article on automotive alternators.

The Engineering Mindset explains that the engine produces only mechanical force, not electricity. The 12-volt lead-acid battery stores energy chemically. With the engine off, the battery runs the electrics and then supplies a very large current to the starter motor. Once the engine runs, the alternator recharges the battery so there is enough energy for the next start, and it powers the electrical devices meanwhile. If a battery is left to discharge too long, it may not turn the starter, and the car will need a jump start.

Pulley: grooved wheel that grips the drive belt from the engine
Shaft and rotor: the rotating electromagnet
Stator: the fixed set of coils in laminated iron, where the current is made
Rectifier: diodes that convert AC to DC
Regulator: limits and steadies the output voltage

Wikipedia adds that typical car alternators use a claw-pole rotor. Its poles look like the fingers of two hands interlocked, and a single coil inside creates a multi-pole magnetic field. Current reaches that coil through slip rings and carbon brushes, and an external fan on the pulley, or fans inside a compact casing, cools the windings.

When the rotor spins, its magnetic field sweeps across the stator windings, which induces alternating current in them. Wikipedia points out the contrast with the old dynamo: in a dynamo the current is generated in the rotating part and converted by a commutator and brushes, but in an alternator it is generated in the stationary stator and converted by diodes.

Cars use direct current, so The Engineering Mindset notes that a rectifier converts the AC to DC. Wikipedia says that a polyphase winding and the shaped rotor poles give a smooth DC output with low ripple.

The faster the engine turns, the more voltage the alternator would produce, so a regulator is needed. Wikipedia explains that it works by changing the small field current to the rotor, which holds a constant voltage at the battery terminals. The field current is far smaller than the output: a 70 A alternator may need only 2 to 3 A. Early regulators were separate devices, later ones sat inside the alternator, and on some modern cars the engine control unit takes over the regulation, using signals such as battery temperature and engine load.

The field coil is first energised from the battery through the ignition switch. Wikipedia says a parallel circuit lights the charge warning lamp, which is why the lamp is on when the ignition is on but the engine is not running. When the alternator starts to generate, it goes out. A burnt-out lamp or a disconnected exciter wire can mean no current reaches the field and the alternator does not generate.
Output and why it replaced the dynamo

Wikipedia says cars used DC dynamos until the 1960s, and as cheap silicon diodes became available the alternator gradually replaced them, helped by growing electrical loads such as larger headlamps, wipers and heated rear windows. Alternators are lighter, cheaper and more rugged, and can deliver useful charge at idle. Chrysler fitted them as standard equipment on the Valiant in 1960, according to the same article.

Typical passenger-car alternators are rated around 50 to 70 A, while large ones on buses or emergency vehicles can reach 300 A. Because an alternator is belt-driven, a loose or worn belt can reduce charging.
This is general information about how the part works. For a charging fault or warning light, have the car inspected by a qualified mechanic.

sources.title: Car Alternator, The Engineering Mindset
Alternator (automotive), Wikipedia

articles.title: Watt-Hours Explained: Laptop Batteries and Flying
articles.excerpt: Laptop and power bank batteries are rated in watt-hours. Learn the volts-times-amp-hours formula and the 100 Wh and 160 Wh limits that airlines apply under US rules.
blocks: A battery's watt-hour (Wh) rating tells you how much energy it stores, and it is the number air safety rules use. You find it by multiplying volts by amp-hours. In the United States, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) allows rechargeable batteries of 0 to 100 Wh on passenger aircraft, requires airline approval for 101 to 160 Wh, and forbids anything above 160 Wh. This article explains the maths and the rules, using the FAA and the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

A watt is a rate of using energy. A watt-hour is that rate sustained for one hour: a 10-watt load running for one hour uses 10 Wh. A bigger Wh figure means a battery can run the same device for longer.
The older rating, milliamp-hours (mAh), only tells you the charge, not the voltage. Two batteries with the same mAh can hold different energy if their voltages differ. Watt-hours remove that problem.

The FAA says a lithium-ion battery's Wh should be marked on it. If not, multiply the volts (V) by the amp-hours (Ah). Its example: a 12-volt battery rated at 8 Ah is 96 Wh, because 12 times 8 is 96. For milliamp-hours, divide by 1,000 to get amp-hours, then multiply by the volts.

Formula: Wh = V x Ah
From mAh: Wh = V x (mAh / 1,000)
Illustration (made-up numbers): a 3.7 V pack of 10,000 mAh gives 3.7 x 10 = 37 Wh
Illustration (made-up numbers): a 15 V laptop battery of 5 Ah gives 75 Wh
The FAA's passenger guidance covers most rechargeable batteries and devices carried for personal use, such as laptops and phones. It sets three bands:

0 to 100 Wh: allowed on passenger aircraft, with no limit on the number of batteries carried for personal use
101 to 160 Wh: needs approval from the air carrier, with a limit of two spare batteries per person
Over 160 Wh: forbidden
The TSA's page on larger batteries says the 101-160 Wh category covers larger after-market laptop batteries and some professional audio and video batteries.
Spares in the cabin, devices powered off

The FAA says spare lithium batteries, including power banks and portable chargers, must be carried on and cannot be checked. A device with a lithium battery can go in checked baggage only if it is completely powered off and protected against accidental activation, and it must still meet the Wh limits.

The FAA explains that all lithium-ion batteries can overheat and undergo thermal runaway, which can happen without warning if the battery is damaged, overheated, exposed to water, overcharged or poorly protected, or on its own because of a manufacturing defect. Flight crews are trained to respond to cabin fires, and the FAA asks passengers to tell the crew straight away if a battery or device is overheating, swelling, smoking or burning. Damaged or recalled batteries must not be taken aboard unless the battery has been removed or made safe.

The FAA warns that many airlines have stricter limits on the number of spare batteries or on Wh. These sources describe United States rules. Other countries' regulators and airlines have their own, so check your airline and departure airport before you travel.

Take a made-up laptop battery marked 11.4 V and 5,000 mAh. Divide 5,000 by 1,000 to get 5 Ah, then multiply by 11.4 volts: 11.4 x 5 = 57 Wh. That is well inside the 100 Wh band. A larger made-up pack of 14.8 V and 8 Ah gives 118.4 Wh, which would fall in the 101 to 160 Wh band and need airline approval under the FAA's guidance.
The numbers in these examples are invented to show the arithmetic. Always use the rating printed on your own battery or in its manual.
This is general information drawn from FAA and TSA pages read on 10 November 2026. Rules can change, so confirm with your airline.

sources.title: Airline Passengers and Batteries, Federal Aviation Administration
Lithium batteries with more than 100 watt hours, Transportation Security Administration

articles.title: How Brushless Motors Drive Electric Scooters
articles.excerpt: Most electric scooters use a brushless DC motor in the wheel hub, switched by an electronic controller. See how it works and how it differs from a brushed motor.
blocks: Most modern electric scooters are driven by a brushless DC (BLDC) motor, often built into the wheel hub. A controller takes direct current from the battery and switches it through coils in turn, so a ring of magnets keeps chasing the rotating field. There are no brushes to wear out. This article explains the parts and the trade-offs, using Wikipedia's articles on brushless motors and electric motorcycles and scooters, and a guide from the scooter maker Levy Electric.

Levy Electric describes the chain this way: the lithium-ion battery supplies DC power, commonly at 36, 48 or 52 volts; an electronic controller manages the voltage and current sent to the motor based on the throttle; the motor turns electrical energy into rotation; and the rotation reaches the wheel. In a hub motor the motor shaft is the axle, so no chain or gears are needed.

Every electric motor needs the current in its coils to change direction as it turns. In a brushed motor, Wikipedia explains, a rotating switch called a commutator does this through carbon brushes that rub against it. Wikipedia lists the drawbacks: friction losses, brush wear that makes dust and eventually needs replacement, voltage drop at the contact, and sparks that can cause electrical interference.

A brushless motor replaces the commutator with electronics. Wikipedia says the construction is similar to a permanent magnet synchronous motor: permanent magnets on the rotor, coils on the fixed stator, and an electronic controller that switches the current. Brushless DC motors became possible with solid-state electronics in the 1960s.
How the controller knows when to switch

The controller must know where the rotor is. Wikipedia says some designs use Hall-effect sensors or a rotary encoder to measure the rotor position directly, while others infer it by measuring back-EMF in the unpowered coils. Levy Electric says Hall sensors are the most common in scooters and check the rotor many times each second.

Magnets on the rotor, coils on the stator
Sensors or back-EMF tell the controller the rotor position
Transistor switches energise the right coils at the right moment
The throttle sets how much current the controller allows

High efficiency: Levy Electric quotes 85 to 90 per cent for modern brushless motors, against 60 to 75 per cent for older brushed ones (a maker's figures)
Low maintenance, since nothing rubs
Quick, precise control of speed and torque
High power for the weight, per Wikipedia
The costs are a more complex controller and a higher price than a brushed motor, as both sources note.

Levy Electric says hub motors are used in the large majority of electric scooters, because they are sealed, quiet and need no chain. Their downside is extra weight in the wheel, which can affect suspension. Mid-drive motors mounted near the centre drive the wheel by chain or belt. They give better weight balance and can use gearing for hills, but need more space and upkeep. The company says they are rare in scooters and more common in electric bicycles. The percentages it gives come from its own guide, not a survey.

Wikipedia records an electric motorcycle announced in 1911 with a claimed range of 75 to 100 miles, and the Peugeot Scoot'Elec of 1996, described as the first mass-produced electric scooter, with nickel-cadmium batteries and a range of 40 km. Wikipedia notes that battery cost and charging speed still limit long-range electric motorcycles.

Because the controller decides when and how current flows, it can also run the motor as a generator when the rider brakes, which sends a little energy back to the battery. Levy Electric lists regenerative braking as a feature possible with gearless hub motors. How much energy comes back depends on the model, speed and battery state.
Efficiency, range and lifetime figures vary by maker and use. Those quoted here come from a scooter manufacturer's guide and Wikipedia, so check a specific model's data sheet.

articles.title: KTM 1390 Super Duke GT EVO Unveiled with AMT Gearbox
articles.excerpt: KTM unveiled the 2027 1390 Super Duke GT EVO at EICMA 2026 with an automated manual gearbox, semi-active suspension and an 8.8-inch TFT. Price and India plans are not announced.
blocks: KTM unveiled the 2027 1390 Super Duke GT EVO at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan in November 2026. It is a higher-spec version of the 1390 Super Duke GT and adds KTM's Automated Manual Transmission (AMT), which lets a rider change gears by hand or leave the shifting to the bike. KTM has not announced a price or any India launch details. This article is correct as of 10 November 2026.

According to Times Drive and Autocar India, the AMT removes the conventional clutch lever. In automatic mode the system changes gear on its own, and the rider can take manual control when they want. Autocar India says the gearbox first appeared on the 1390 Super Adventure S Evo. It is still a manual gearbox with electronic actuation, so the six speeds listed on KTM's specification page remain.

KTM's specification page lists a 1,350 cc, liquid-cooled, 75-degree V-twin with 145 Nm of torque and a 6-speed transmission. Autocar India states 187 hp; KTM's page does not list power in the section reviewed, and other reports have used figures near 190 hp, so treat any single power number with care.

Frame: chromium-molybdenum steel trellis, with a single-sided swingarm (Autocar India)
Suspension: third-generation WP APEX semi-active, 48 mm front fork and a linked rear shock (KTM)
Travel: 125 mm front and 140 mm rear (KTM)
Brakes: two Brembo Stylema four-piston monobloc front calipers on 320 mm discs; 240 mm rear disc (KTM)
Wheels and tyres: 17-inch front and rear, Michelin Power 6 tyres (Autocar India)

Weight without fuel: 213 kg (KTM)
Seat height: 834 mm (KTM)
Wheelbase: 1,491 mm (KTM)
Fuel tank: about 19 litres (KTM)
Ground clearance: 149 mm (KTM)
Autocar India says the lighter 17-inch wheels save 1.2 kg compared with the standard Super Duke GT.

Times Drive reports four standard riding modes (Rain, Street, Sport and Custom) with an optional Track Mode that adds launch control and adjustable anti-wheelie settings. Autocar India lists traction control, a quickshifter and ABS among the electronics. The bike has an 8.8-inch TFT touchscreen with offline map navigation, and Times Drive adds route planning and a USB-C port.

The lighting package includes cornering lights and daytime running lights. Times Drive also mentions a Coming Home function. For touring, the reports list an adjustable windscreen, a repositionable handlebar and redesigned rider and passenger seats.
Availability and what is not known

Autocar India says the bike is expected at dealerships in early 2027 globally. Times Drive says KTM has not announced a price and has not shared India launch or availability details. For context only, Times Drive's page lists the KTM 1390 Super Duke R at Rs 22.95 lakh ex-showroom in India; that is a different model, and it says nothing about the GT EVO's price.
How it relates to other KTM models

Autocar India describes the GT EVO as a higher-spec variant of the standard 1390 Super Duke GT, sharing its V-twin with the 1390 Super Adventure S Evo. Compared with the Adventure model's 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wheels, the sport-tourer uses 17-inch wheels at both ends. Times Drive adds that KTM says the updated frame has three times the torsional stiffness of the previous 1290 Super Duke GT, and that the front fork uses a patented through-rod construction. Those are manufacturer claims and were not tested for this article.

Because the sources differ on the power figure and KTM has not published a price, this article does not compare the GT EVO with rival sport-tourers on cost or output. When KTM publishes market-specific details, those will be the figures to use.

KTM's global press release could not be opened. The specification figures are from KTM's own technical page for the UAE market, and the descriptions come from Times Drive and Autocar India. Figures may differ by market.
